title: Prime-to-p normalization and descent of critical cosets
statement:
Let $k\subseteq F$ be complete fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values, with $k$ algebraically closed. For a valued field $H$ put $H^\circ=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde H=H^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_H=|H^	imes|$. Let $p=\operatorname{char}\widetilde k>0$. For $a,b\in F$, $s>0$ put $S_{a,s}(F)=\{c^p-ac+e:c,e\in F,\ |pc^p|<s,\ |e|<s\}$. Use the same formula for $S_{A,t}(H)$ in any valued extension $H$ and any coefficient $A$ and threshold $t>0$. Suppose $C=b+S_{a,s}(F)$ is critical, meaning $0
otin C$ and $\inf_{v\in C}|v|=s$. If $a=0$ put $E=F$, $\alpha=1$ and $A=0$. If $a
e0$, choose $\alpha^{p-1}=a$ in an algebraic closure, put $E=F(\alpha)$ with the extending absolute value, and put $A=1$. Then $E$ is complete and $E/F$ is finite tame: with $e=[\Gamma_E:\Gamma_F]$, $f=[\widetilde E:\widetilde F]$, one has $[E:F]=ef$, $\widetilde E/\widetilde F$ is separable and $p
mid e$; in fact $[E:F]$ divides $p-1$. Set $B=b/\alpha^p$ and $t=s/|\alpha|^p$. The coset $C^\prime=B+S_{A,t}(E)$ is critical. If $C^\prime$ has an element of absolute value $t$, then $C$ has an element of absolute value $s$.

source.place: Agent-supplied coefficient normalization and normalized-trace descent supplement to the first paragraph of the proof of Proposition 6.2.4, printed p. 47; scaling as in Proposition 6.1.4(ii), printed p. 38. proof.text: Compatibility of the absolute values gives $k^\circ=F^\circ\cap k$ and $\{x\in k:|x|<1\}=\{x\in F:|x|<1\}\cap k$. Therefore the induced map $\widetilde k\to\widetilde F$ is injective, so $\operatorname{char}\widetilde F=p$. For $a\ne0$ put $m=p-1$. The residue of $m$ is $-1$, so $|m|=1$ and $m$ is invertible in $F$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, $X^m-1$ splits over $k$ and hence over $F$. Apply the multiradical degree lemma with one radical, exponent $m$, and radicand $a$: $E/F$ is finite Galois and $[E:F]\mid p-1$. For $a=0$, $E=F$ has degree one, also dividing $p-1$. Thus in both cases $n=[E:F]$ is prime to $p$.

source.place: Agent supplement to Proposition 6.1.4(ii), normalization by a (p-1)-st root

proof.text: The finite ramification calculus gives completeness of $E$ for the extending absolute value. For $a\ne0$, apply the root-envelope characterization with $K=F$, $L=E$, $U=F$ and the single radical $\alpha^{p-1}=a$. All $(p-1)$-st roots of unity lie in $k\subseteq F$ as above. The identity $F^\circ\to F^\circ$ is finite etale: it is free of rank one and every lifting problem for the identity has exactly one lift. Therefore condition (b) of that characterization holds, so condition (a) gives $[E:F]=ef$, separability of the residue extension and $p\nmid e$. For $a=0$ these conclusions hold with $e=f=1$.

source.place: Section 2.1, Lemma 2.1.5(iii); radical formulation of the tame extension used in Proposition 6.1.4(ii)

proof.text: Put $D=b+S_{a,s}(E)$. The map $w\mapsto w/\alpha^p$ gives a bijection $D\to C^\prime$: write $d=\alpha c$ and $e=\alpha^p e^\prime$, and compute $$\alpha^{-p}(d^p-ad+e)=c^p-Ac+e^\prime,\quad |pd^p|<s\ \Longleftrightarrow\ |pc^p|<t,\quad |e|<s\ \Longleftrightarrow\ |e^\prime|<t.$$ Indeed $a\alpha/\alpha^p=A$, including $a=0$, $\alpha=1$. Absolute values under this bijection are divided by $|\alpha|^p$.

Use the degree-normalized trace $T:E\to F$ of the trace-bound lemma; step 1 supplies its Galois, residue-characteristic and prime-to-$p$ hypotheses, and step 2 supplies completeness. For $w=b+d^p-ad+e\in D$ with $|pd^p|<s$ and $|e|<s$, set $c=T(d)$ and $$\epsilon=T(e)+T(d^p)-T(d)^p.$$ Then $T(w)=b+c^p-ac+\epsilon$. The two trace estimates give $|pc^p|\le|p|\,|d|^p<s$ and $$|\epsilon|\le\max(|e|,|p|\,|d|^p)<s.$$ Hence $T(w)\in C$ and $|T(w)|\le|w|$. This calculation also applies in equal characteristic, where the Frobenius error is zero.

source.place: Agent normalized-trace descent supplement to Proposition 6.2.4, proof, printed p. 47

proof.text: Since $\inf_{v\in C}|v|=s$, every $T(w)\in C$ satisfies $|T(w)|\ge s$. Step 4 therefore gives $|w|\ge s$ for every $w\in D$. Conversely $C\subseteq D$, so $\inf_{w\in D}|w|\le s$. Thus $\inf_{w\in D}|w|=s$ and $0\notin D$ because $s>0$. The scaling bijection in step 3 proves that $C^\prime$ is critical. Finally, if $v^\prime\in C^\prime$ has $|v^\prime|=t$, put $w=\alpha^p v^\prime\in D$. Then $|w|=s$ and $T(w)\in C$ has $s\le|T(w)|\le s$, proving the required descent of a minimum.

source.place: Agent infimum and minimum descent supplement to Proposition 6.2.4, proof, printed p. 47
